description: Each city's count is its number of driver qualifying entries, and its share is its share of all qualifying entries.

b.request: Which circuit cities have an above-average share of qualifying entries? For each city, show the city name, its count of driver qualifying entries (qualifying rows joined to races and circuits, grouped by circuits.location), that count divided by the total qualifying entries across all cities, and that share minus the average per-city share, with all values unrounded
b.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS entries FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON q.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY c.location), shares AS (SELECT city, entries, entries * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(entries) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city, s.entries, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_diff FROM shares s, avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

a.request: For each circuit city (`circuits.location`), count the qualifying records (one per driver per race) at races held there, and work out the city's share as that count divided by the total across all cities. List the cities whose share is above the average share across cities, showing the city, the count, the share, and how far the share is above the average share, all unrounded.
a.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS cnt FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON q.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId WHERE c.location IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.location), shares AS (SELECT city, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city, s.cnt AS count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_average FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY s.share DESC;

c.request: Which circuit cities have an above-average share of qualifying? For each, show the city, its qualifying count, that count as a share of the total across all cities, and how far its share is above the average city share (all unrounded). Each city's count is its number of driver qualifying entries, and its share is its share of all qualifying entries.
c.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON q.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY c.location), shares AS (SELECT city, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM city_counts) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city AS city, s.cnt AS qualifying_count, s.share AS share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_average_by FROM shares s, avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY above_average_by DESC;

d.request: Which circuit cities have an above-average share of qualifying, where each city's count is its number of driver qualifying entries and its share is that count as a fraction of all qualifying entries across all cities? For each, show the city, its qualifying count, that count as a share of the total, and how far its share is above the average city share (all unrounded).
d.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT c.location AS city, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON q.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY c.location), totals AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM city_counts), shares AS (SELECT city, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT total FROM totals) AS share FROM city_counts), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.city, s.cnt AS qualifying_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS above_avg_by FROM shares s, avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share ORDER BY above_avg_by DESC;
